If the intent is to **enforce** `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` repo-wide (no project may opt out), then keeping it in `.targets` is intentional — but it should be documented and the dead code in LibB removed.

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13 — Unquoted `Condition` value (AP-05)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** Both sides of the condition are unquoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty or unset (e.g., during evaluation from the IDE or a bare `dotnet build` without explicit configuration), MSBuild evaluates the raw expression `== Debug` which silently evaluates to `false` instead of erroring. The correct idiomatic form quotes both sides.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14 — `DefineConstants` overwritten instead of appended (AP-09)

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** all existing define constants. The SDK sets `TRACE` (and `DEBUG` in Debug configuration) by default. After this line, those are gone — `#if TRACE` and `#if DEBUG` blocks become dead code. This is a silent semantic bug.

**Fix:**
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

### 5. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45 — Self-referencing `<MSBuild>` task forks a second build instance (AP-22)

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish"
           Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This re-invokes the same project with an additional global property (`_IsPublishing=true`), which creates a **second evaluation instance** of the project. Both instances share the same `OutputPath` and `IntermediateOutputPath`, so they race on writing the same files — causing intermittent build failures, especially in parallel builds (`-m`). The Publish target also re-runs Build internally, doubling the work.

**Fix:** Remove this target entirely and publish explicitly (`dotnet publish`), or restructure using `DependsOnTargets` to stay in the same evaluation:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);_PublishAfterBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="_PublishAfterBuild" Condition="'$(PublishOnBuild)' == 'true'">
  <!-- Run publish logic in the same instance -->
</Target>
```

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9 — Wrong F# source file order

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />   <!-- depends on Domain -->
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     <!-- defines types used by Services -->
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** F# compilation is **order-dependent** — files can only reference types defined in files listed *above* them. `Services.fs` opens `BrokenOrder.Domain` (defined in `Domain.fs`), but `Domain.fs` is listed *after* `Services.fs`. This will fail to compile with an error like `The namespace or module 'BrokenOrder.Domain' is not defined`.

Compare with the correctly ordered `OrderService.fsproj`:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     <!-- ✅ Domain first -->
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />   <!-- ✅ Services second -->
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Fix:**
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 7. `Directory.Build.props`, line 17 — Analyzer package missing `PrivateAssets="all"` (AP-17)

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Analyzer packages should not flow transitively to consumers. Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, any project that references LibA or LibB as a package will also get StyleCop.Analyzers imposed on them — an unwanted side effect.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** This path is Windows-specific and machine-specific. It will fail on Linux/macOS CI, and it will conflict with other developers' environments. The same issue appears in `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 7.

**Fix:** Use relative paths or SDK conventions:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\artifacts\LibA\</OutputPath>
```
Or better yet, use the modern `ArtifactsPath` property in .NET 8+ which handles this automatically.

---

### 9. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 21–24 — Redundant `Include` + `Update` on SDK-globbed item (AP-12)

```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```

**Problem:** The SDK already auto-includes `*.cs` files. The explicit `<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />` creates a **duplicate** entry — MSBuild will pass the file to the compiler twice, producing warning **CS2002** ("Source file specified multiple times"). The `Update` is fine on its own.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` line; keep only the `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 10. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–30 — Legacy assembly `<Reference>` with hardcoded `HintPath` (AP-04)

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-style reference in an SDK-style project. It uses a hardcoded path to a version-specific, TFM-specific DLL under a `packages/` folder that doesn't even exist in this repo. It will fail on restore and won't participate in NuGet dependency resolution.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper `PackageReference`:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 11. No Central Package Management (CPM) configured

Package versions are scattered across individual files (`Directory.Build.props` line 17 for StyleCop, and the legacy reference in LibA). As the solution grows, version drift becomes likely.

**Fix:** Create a `Directory.Packages.props` at the repo root:
```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemDefinitionGroup>
    <!-- Define all versions here -->
  </ItemDefinitionGroup>
</Project>
```

<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
